chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi, from al-Amriki al-Bufaki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who made it a vow upon himself for the sake of Allah to pray such and such a prayer; is it sufficient for him to pray that while riding his mount, and he is a traveler? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.جَعَلَ لِلَّهِ عَلَيْهِ: made a vow upon himself for the sake of Allah

ai.seo_question: Can a traveler fulfill a vow to pray specific prayers while riding their mount?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies that a vow to perform specific prayers is fulfilled by praying while riding (Salat al-Musafir) during travel, as the act of prayer itself is the core obligation rather than the specific posture. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence (Fiqh) regarding vows (Nudhur), ensuring that travelers are not burdened with dismounting unnecessarily, thereby preserving the ease (Yusr) intended by Sharia. It underscores the principle that the validity of the vow depends on the completion of the prescribed prayer unit, regardless of the physical position dictated by the traveler's state.
